newsitem.title: UK: Gold touch stronger, but still under gloomy cloud.
newsitem.headline: Gold touch stronger, but still under gloomy cloud.

text.p: Gold held near the top of its recent range on Friday morning, supported by buying in the white metals, but gloomy sentiment was expected to soon pull the market down to fresh lows, dealers said.
"I don't think the gold market is out of the woods yet," a senior dealer said.
Gold fixed at $354.10 per ounce, up $1.05 from Thursday afternoon, with the spot market holding around the New York close of $354.35/$354.85.
Spot gold bids were indicated as high as $355.20, the third day the market has been capped around the $355 level.
The bottom end of the recent range has been the fresh 3-1/4 lows around $351.50 touched on Wednesday.
Important support levels were pegged at the psychological $350 area, $345 and then $330.
"If prices don't close tonight above $355 or $356, I think we could see more weakness," a dealer said. "There's no news, no incentive for anyone to buy gold."

The fear of more central bank sales was still overhanging the market, while interest rates were muted, giving a further kick to galloping stock markets that have been regularly notching up fresh records.
The UK's FTSE index of 100 leading shares breached the 4,200 level for the first time on Friday morning after a strong close on Wall Street the previous evening.
Traders in Asia say physical gold demand has been fairly strong, with a shortage of kilo bars appearing in Hong Kong.
But dealers in London said this was unlikely to stem the downward momentum. "Physical demand overall is steady but not huge," one said.
Writers of put options are not fully covered and any probing at new lows would spark delta hedging, accelerating any slide, option dealers said.
Silver bumped higher to $4.76/$4.78, up about four cents from Thursday's London close.
The market sees upside potential in silver, but it is divided over whether the metal can struggle higher while gold is still under a cloud of bearish sentiment.
"I think it will have to move back to the $4.50s before it can really move higher," one dealer said.
Platinum was up about $1.00 at $360.25/$361.25 while palladium was around $2.00 firmer $122.75/$123.75.
